title: Time & timers
summary: Clocks, sleeps, POSIX timers, alarm and the interval timers keep and measure time as POSIX requires, on every target.

cases.title: clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME) succeeds with tv_nsec below one second and a date between 2020 and 2100
clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) succeeds with a nonnegative time and tv_nsec below one second
CLOCK_MONOTONIC never goes backwards over 100000 reads in one thread
CLOCK_MONOTONIC never goes backwards between threads running on two processors
Linux policy: CLOCK_MONOTONIC advances between consecutive reads rather than once per tick
CLOCK_REALTIME and CLOCK_MONOTONIC advance at the same rate over 2 seconds
CLOCK_MONOTONIC advances at the rate of the processor's counter over 2 seconds (ARM64 CNTVCT_EL0, x86-64 the TSC at its CPUID frequency)
Linux ABI: CLOCK_REALTIME advances at the rate of the RTC, read through /dev/rtc0 RTC_RD_TIME, over 3 seconds
CLOCK_PROCESS_CPUTIME_ID advances while the process computes and not while it sleeps
CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID counts only the calling thread's CPU time
clock_gettime of an unknown clock fails with EINVAL
Linux policy: clock_gettime into an unmapped buffer fails with EFAULT
clock_getres reports a resolution above zero and no coarser than 20 ms for the realtime, monotonic and CPU-time clocks
clock_getres with a null resolution pointer succeeds
clock_getres of an unknown clock fails with EINVAL
Linux policy: CLOCK_MONOTONIC_COARSE reports the kernel tick as its resolution and advances in steps of it (5 ms on x86-64, 1 ms on ARM64)
clock_settime(CLOCK_REALTIME) sets the clock to the nanosecond value given and CLOCK_MONOTONIC does not jump
clock_settime by an unprivileged process fails with EPERM and leaves CLOCK_REALTIME unchanged
clock_settime with tv_nsec out of range, on CLOCK_MONOTONIC or on an unknown clock fails with EINVAL
gettimeofday succeeds and agrees with CLOCK_REALTIME to the microsecond
time() returns CLOCK_REALTIME's seconds and stores them through its argument
nanosleep of 100 ms returns 0 no earlier than 100 ms later, late by at most two ticks and 20 ms
nanosleep of 1 s and 250000000 ns sleeps the whole of both
Twenty 1 ms nanosleeps each end no earlier than 1 ms, with a median late by at most one tick and 1 ms
nanosleep of zero returns 0 at once
nanosleep with tv_nsec below 0 or at least 1000000000, or a negative tv_sec, fails with EINVAL at once
Linux policy: nanosleep with an unmapped request fails with EFAULT
A caught signal ends nanosleep early with EINTR and writes the time left to rem
Calling nanosleep again with rem after EINTR completes the sleep first asked for
Linux policy: nanosleep fails with EINTR after a handler even with SA_RESTART
A signal that is ignored does not end nanosleep
A blocked signal does not end nanosleep and stays pending
A sleeper stopped and continued by SIGSTOP and SIGCONT finishes its nanosleep, neither early nor with EINTR
Four threads sleeping 200 to 500 ms at once each wake on time
clock_nanosleep on CLOCK_MONOTONIC for 100 ms sleeps no less, late by at most two ticks and 20 ms
clock_nanosleep on CLOCK_REALTIME for 100 ms sleeps no less, late by at most two ticks and 20 ms
clock_nanosleep with TIMER_ABSTIME on CLOCK_MONOTONIC wakes no earlier than the deadline and late by at most two ticks and 20 ms
clock_nanosleep with TIMER_ABSTIME on CLOCK_REALTIME wakes no earlier than the deadline and late by at most two ticks and 20 ms
clock_nanosleep with TIMER_ABSTIME and a deadline already past returns 0 at once
A caught signal ends a relative clock_nanosleep with EINTR and the time left in rem
A caught signal ends an absolute clock_nanosleep with EINTR and leaves rem untouched
clock_nanosleep with tv_nsec out of range, an unknown clock or the caller's thread CPU-time clock fails with EINVAL
Setting CLOCK_REALTIME past an absolute CLOCK_REALTIME sleep's deadline wakes it
Setting CLOCK_REALTIME forward does not shorten a nanosleep
Setting CLOCK_REALTIME forward does not shorten a relative clock_nanosleep on CLOCK_REALTIME
A CLOCK_MONOTONIC timer with SIGEV_SIGNAL delivers its signal on time with si_code SI_TIMER and its sigev_value
A timer created with no sigevent delivers SIGALRM with the timer ID as its value
A SIGEV_NONE timer sends no signal, and timer_gettime shows it count down and expire
A CLOCK_REALTIME timer fires on time
timer_create with an unknown clock, signal 0 or 65, or an unknown sigev_notify fails with EINVAL
A one-shot timer fires once, on time, and then reads as disarmed
A periodic 50 ms timer fires twenty times a second, 50 ms apart
timer_gettime reports the time left, decreasing and never above the value set, and the interval
timer_settime returns the previous setting in old_value
timer_settime with a zero it_value disarms the timer
A timer armed with TIMER_ABSTIME fires no earlier than that time and late by at most two ticks and 20 ms
A timer armed with TIMER_ABSTIME for a time already past fires at once
timer_settime with tv_nsec out of range or on an unknown timer fails with EINVAL
timer_getoverrun and si_overrun count the expiries a pending timer signal stood for
The overrun count starts again from zero once the timer's signal is delivered
timer_delete disarms the timer, and its ID then fails with EINVAL
Eight timers get distinct IDs and each delivers its own value, in expiry order
A CLOCK_PROCESS_CPUTIME_ID timer counts the process's CPU time, not time asleep
A CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID timer counts the calling thread's CPU time, not time asleep
A child created by fork inherits none of its parent's timers
exec deletes the caller's timers: their IDs are invalid in the new program and they never fire
alarm(1) delivers SIGALRM no earlier than one second later, late by at most two ticks and 20 ms
SIGALRM from alarm terminates a process that has not caught it
alarm returns the seconds left of the previous alarm
alarm(0) cancels a pending alarm and returns the seconds it had left
A new alarm replaces the old one: only the new one fires
An alarm interrupts a blocking read of an empty pipe with EINTR
setitimer ITIMER_REAL with no interval fires SIGALRM once, on time
ITIMER_REAL reloads its interval: a 50 ms timer fires twenty times a second, 50 ms apart
getitimer reports the time left, decreasing and never above the value set, and the interval
setitimer returns the previous setting in old_value
setitimer with a zero it_value disarms the timer
An ITIMER_REAL value of one microsecond still fires
setitimer and getitimer of an unknown timer, and setitimer with tv_usec out of range, fail with EINVAL
Linux policy: alarm and setitimer ITIMER_REAL are one timer
ITIMER_VIRTUAL counts user CPU time: no SIGVTALRM while the process sleeps, one while it computes
ITIMER_VIRTUAL reloads its interval while the process computes
ITIMER_PROF counts CPU time: no SIGPROF while the process sleeps, one while it computes
fork clears the child's alarm and interval timers and leaves the parent's armed
exec keeps the time left until an alarm, and the alarm fires in the new program
Linux policy: exec keeps ITIMER_VIRTUAL and ITIMER_PROF
